{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-markov}
#### Markov's inequality

Let $X$ be a random variable with $X \ge 0$ and $\E{X} < \infty$.
Then for every $a > 0$:

$$
\Prf{X \ge a} \le \frac{\E{X}}{a}
$$

:::

::: proof

Because $X \ge 0$, every outcome satisfies $X \ge a \cdot \indic{\set{X \ge a}}$:
when $X \ge a$ the right side is $a \le X$, and otherwise it is $0 \le X$.
The expectation of a nonnegative random variable is nonnegative,
so by [linearity of expectation](expectation.qmd#thm-linearity-expectation),
and because the expectation of an indicator is the probability of its event,

$$
\E{X} - a \cdot \Prf{X \ge a}
= \E{X - a \cdot \indic{\set{X \ge a}}}
\ge 0
$$

and dividing by $a > 0$ gives the claim.

:::
